sentences.text: Heard Sri Amit Kumar and Sri Amar Nath Dubey, Advocates, the learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Rajiv Kuamr Verma, learned Addl. Government Advocate, Sri Onkar Nath Nishad, the learned counsel for the informant, and perused the record.

2. By means of the instant application the applicant Sanjay Sonkar prays for anticipatory bail in Case Crime No. 0078 of 2023, under Sections 376, 506, I.P.C., and Section 3/4, the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, P.S. Hasanganj, District Lucknow.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. The aforesaid case has been registered on the basis of an F.I.R. lodged on 25.05.2023 alleging that in January, 2023 the applicant had called the informant, who is aged about 14 years, to his shop and he raped her in his go-down on pistol point.
The F.I.R. states that the injured did not disclose this fact at that time and now she is pregnant.

sentences.text: In the affidavit filed in support of the bail-application it has been stated that the applicant is innocent and he has falsely been implicated in the present case.
In para-15 the affidavit it has been stated that the applicant is ready for his medical-examination as well as D.N.A. test.

Prior to lodging of the instant F.I.R., the informant herself had lodged another F.I.R. bearing Case Crime No. 0042 of 2023 under sections 354, 354(A),506, I.P.C. and section 7/8, the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, P.S. Hasanganj, District Lucknow, against one Salman Mirza on 12.03.2023, alleging that she works in a Pet Clinic and on 11.03.2023 the named accused had molested her in the Clinic.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 5. This application was filed on 19.06.2023.
On 26.06.2023, time was granted for filing objection/counter affidavit.
The case was adjourned on 04.07.2023.
On 13.07.2023, the State has granted 48 hours' time for filing a counter affidavit, but the State has filed the counter affidavit today only.
6. Copies of the statements recorded during investigation, a copy of the medical report, Forensic Science Laboratory report etc. have been annexed with the counter affidavit filed by the State.

The applicant's involvement in another case bearing Case Crime No. 347 of 2004 under Sections 147,
323, 504, 506, I.P.C., P.S. Hasanganj, District Lucknow, has also been disclosed, in which chargesheet has been submitted on 14.12.2004.
7.
The informant has also filed a counter affidavit annexing therewith her ultrasonography-report and marks-sheet to prove her age and her pregnancy, which facts are not disputed.

However,
nothing has been stated in the counter affidavit in reply to the statements made in the affidavit filed in support of the bail-application that the applicant is innocent and he is ready to get his medical-examination and D.N.A. test conducted to ascertain the correctness of the allegations.
8. A rejoinder affidavit has been filed by the applicant in reply to the counter affidavit filed by the informant.

9. Although the applicant has directly approached this Court for grant of Anticipatory Bail, without first approaching the Sessions Judge, no objection in this regard has been raised either in the counter affidavit filed by the State or by the informant, nor has any such objection been raised during submissions.
10.

In para-6 of the affidavit, filed in support of the bail-application, the applicant has stated that the local police is continuously threatening and trying to arrest the applicant and normally the Sessions Court rejects the anticipatory bail applications, in cases involving offences alleged against the applicant.
11. No reply to this statement has been given in the counter affidavit filed by the informant.
12. The State has also not raised any objection against the application directly having been filed before this Court.
The anticipatory bail-application is pending before this Court since 19.06.2023 and a period of more than one month has already elapsed.

sentences.text:
In Ankit Bharti v. State of U.P., 2020 SCCOnline Alld. 1949 a larger Bench of this Court approved the following conclusions recorded by an Hon'ble Single Judge in Vinod Kumar v. State of U.P., 2019 (12) ADJ 495:
"A. Section 438 Cr. P.C. on its plain terms does not mandate or require a party to first approach the Sessions Court before applying to the High Court for grant of anticipatory bail.

entities.text: Ankit Bharti v. State of U.P., 2020 SCCOnline Alld. 1949
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Vinod Kumar v. State of U.P., 2019 (12) ADJ 495
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The provision as it stands does not require an individual first being relegated to the Court of Sessions before being granted the right of audience before this Court.

B. Notwithstanding concurrent jurisdiction being conferred on the High Court and the Court of Session for grant of anticipatory bail under Section 438 Cr. P.C., strong,
cogent, compelling and special circumstances must necessarily be found to exist in justification of the High Court being approached first without the avenue as available before the Court of Sessions being exhausted.
Whether those factors are established or found to exist in the facts of a particular case must necessarily be left for the Court to consider in each individual matter.

C. The words "exceptional" or "extraordinary" are understood to mean atypical, rare,
out of the ordinary, unusual or uncommon.

If the jurisdiction of the Court as conferred by Section 438 Cr. P.C. be circumscribed or be recognised to be moved only in exceptional situations it would again amount to fettering and constricting the discretion otherwise conferred by Section 438 Cr. P.C.
Such a construction would be in clear conflict of the statutory mandate.

The ratio of Harendra Singh must be recognised to be the requirement of establishing the existence of special, weighty and compelling reasons and circumstances justifying the invocation of the jurisdiction of this Court even though a wholesome avenue of redress was available before the Court of Sessions.

D. What would constitute "special circumstances" in light of the nature of the power conferred must be left to be gathered by the Judge on a due evaluation of the facts and circumstances of a particular case.
It would be imprudent to exhaustively chronicle what would be special circumstances.
It is impossible to either identify or compendiously postulate what would constitute special circumstances.
Sibbia spoke of the "Imperfect awareness of the needs of new situations".
It is this constraint which necessitates the Court leaving it to the wisdom of the Judge and the discretion vested in him by statute.

E. While the Explanation may have created an avenue for an aggrieved person to challenge an order passed under Section 438 (1), it cannot be construed or viewed as barring the jurisdiction of the High Court from entertaining an application for grant of anticipatory bail notwithstanding that prayer having been refused by the Court of Sessions.

3 F.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Till such time as the question with respect to the period for which an order under Section 438 Cr. P.C. should operate is answered by the Larger Bench, the Court granting anticipatory bail would have to specify that it would continue only till the Court summons the accused based on the report that may be submitted under Section 173(2) Cr. P.C. whereafter it would be open for the applicant on appearance to seek regular bail in accordance with the provisions made in Section 439 Cr. P.C."
14.
The Larger Bench held that "the conclusions recorded in the Vinod Kumar (supra), on the meaning to be ascribed to exceptional or special circumstances needs no re-consideration.

It must,
as was noted there, be left to the concerned Judge to exercise the discretion, as vested in him by the statute depending upon the facts obtaining in a particular case."

15. The application is pending before this Court since 19.06.2023 and a period of more than one month has already elapsed; that the State as also the informant have filed counter affidavits and they have not raised any preliminary objection regarding the applicant directly having approached this court, without his approaching the Sessions Judge and no such objection has been raised even during submissions.
The respondents have advanced their submissions on merits of the application.

Therefore, I am of the view that the aforesaid facts make out a special circumstance for the application being considered and decided on its merits, without relegating the applicant to the Sessions Judge, therefore, I proceed to consider the merits of the application.
16. From the material collected during investigation it is undisputed that the victim/informant is a minor and she is pregnant.

17. Having considered the facts and circumstances of the case, what prma facie appears from the material available on record before the Court at this stage is that the incident allegedly took place in the month of January 2023.

The informant herself had filed an F.I.R. under Sections 354,
354(A),506, I.P.C. and Section 7/8, the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012,
against another person Salman Mirza on 12.03.2023 alleging that Salman Mirza had molested her on 11.03.2023, which, prima facie indicates that the informant is well aware that physical abuse of any degree is an offence, particularly if committed against a child, and that she can file an F.I.R.
against the person, who has committed offences under I.P.C. and POCSO Act.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 18. The F.I.R. against the applicant has been lodged on 25.05.2023 regarding an incident which allegedly took place in January, 2023.

However, she did not choose to file an F.I.R. of her rape,
allegedly committed in January, 2023 promptly, whereas she had promptly lodged an F.I.R. of molestation within 24 hours of the incident.

19. Keeping in view the aforesaid facts, coupled with the fact that the applicant has categorically stated that he is ready to get his D.N.A. examination conducted and no reply to this has been given in the counter affidavit filed by the State as also by the informant, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be granted anticipatory bail.
